title: Technical Support Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build operating-system and networking fundamentals first, then add troubleshooting, scripting, cloud, databases, security and customer-facing incident management.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and ending around 2030. The semester milestones can be shifted to match the university calendar.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Linux/Windows, networking, troubleshooting, scripting, databases, ticketing, documentation and customer communication.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Cloud support, application support, infrastructure support, network support, SaaS support or security operations.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Advanced incident management, automation, reliability, root-cause analysis, architecture and technical ownership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Platform/SRE work, support engineering leadership, cloud architecture, automation, security and technical strategy.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If you take the four-year honours/research variant, use the additional year for distributed systems, cloud support automation, observability, cybersecurity, SRE or a substantial infrastructure/support engineering project.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move from resolving individual tickets to preventing recurring incidents. Learn automation, observability, root-cause analysis, cloud infrastructure and security so that you can improve the systems behind the support workload.

blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: These are typical stages, not guaranteed promotion dates.
PhD routes

Progress from reactive support toward engineering ownership. Automate recurring issues, improve observability and reliability, contribute to architecture decisions and develop expertise in cloud, security or platform engineering. Technical leadership can eventually include support-engineering management or a senior individual-contributor infrastructure role.
